column1: # Tracked copy of the parity divergence table (round 2: 131 scenarios = 87 MATCH + 44 EXPECTED-DIVERGENCE + 0 UNEXPECTED).
# Read by Code/Development/Parity/compare.py; the prose version is divergences_Explained.md in this folder.
# Quirk ids (Q2..Q33) are rows of Project_Manag/Docs/Descr/behavior_Contract.md; "rust_Rewrite.md §N" points to
# Project_Manag/Docs/Decisions/rust_Rewrite.md. Q31 (symlinked or .. scan root), Q32 (empty or nonexistent config entries) and Q33 (apply or
# delete through a symlinked .agents) were added to the contract after the replays of rounds 1 and 2 showed them.
# covers: comma list of check kinds this entry explains: exit[=N|M], tree[=pre], set, rest
#   exit=3     the Rust exit code must be 3 (else the entry does not cover it -> UNEXPECTED)
#   tree=pre   Rust's projects tree after the step must equal its tree before the step
# a scenario whose differing checks are all covered is EXPECTED-DIVERGENCE

column4: Steps 1 and 2 (root: "" and a bare root:) match (Go needs the Setup TUI, Rust exits 3). Step 3: with an explicit --root, Go ignores the empty config value and works; Rust still rejects the config ('root must not be empty', exit 3). Intended: a config file is checked whenever it is read, even when a flag overrides the key (Q32).
Go ignores a malformed config.yaml (contract §2); Rust parses with deny_unknown_fields and fails with line/column, exit 3. Nothing written.
Go: no error, prints 'No matching skills found' (exit 0). Rust: hard error 'scan root is not a directory' (exit 3). Q12 was UNCLEAR; policy 'hard errors, no fallbacks'.

Step 1: `--root link` (symlink, no trailing slash). Go's WalkDir does not descend, so nothing is found; Rust resolves the root to its canonical path and finds all 12 targets. Step 2 (trailing slash) agrees; Rust prints the canonical paths (<TMP>/projects/...) where Go prints the link spelling (<TMP>/projects_link/...), which the set comparison maps.
delete coding --root link: without the trailing slash Go finds nothing (exit 0); Rust canonicalizes the root and deletes from all 4 projects. Step 2 agrees.
Go: exit 0 with 'No matching skills found'. Rust: hard error 'scan root does not exist' (exit 3).

The scenario's empty vault dir is not a git repo, so Rust fails with 'not a git repository' (exit 3); Go printed 'No skills found in vault.' (exit 0). The empty GIT vault is covered by cfg_vault_git_zero_skills (MATCH).
Go removes the whole .agents/skills dir. Rust rejects '.' as a skill name (exit 2); tree untouched.
Go removes the whole .agents dir. Rust rejects '..' (exit 2); tree untouched.
Go removes the whole .agents/skills dir. Rust rejects the empty name (exit 2); tree untouched.
Go finds nothing and exits 0. Rust rejects the empty name (usage error, exit 2) before scanning.
Go prints 'deleted from' for a skill the project does not have (exit 0). Rust: 'is not an installed skill folder', exit 3, nothing touched.
Go prints 'deleted from' for a project path that does not exist (exit 0). Rust: 'is not an installed skill folder', exit 3.

Go's RemoveAll follows the .agents symlink and deletes real_agents/skills/coding outside the project (rest.manifest differs). Rust: '.agents is a symlink; skill folders behind a link are never removed', exit 3, nothing deleted.
Same through a symlinked .agents/skills: Go deletes inside the link target, Rust refuses (exit 3).

Go removes what it can (languages/*) and leaves the rest, prints the error but exits 0 and counts the project as updated. Rust renames the folder into .agents/.trash-* first; on a read-only folder that rename fails with EACCES, so the skill stays complete (no .trash-* left); other projects are deleted, exit 4 (partial).
Go removes languages/* then fails (exit 1). Rust's rename into .agents/.trash-* fails with EACCES, the skill stays complete, exit 4 (partial).
Go removes a subfolder of the skill. Rust rejects names with a separator (exit 2); tree untouched.
Go deletes <project>/src through '../../src'. Rust rejects the name (exit 2); tree untouched.
mandatory = [ghost, coding]. Go silently drops 'ghost' and pushes coding. Rust refuses the whole push (exit 3, nothing written) and names the unknown skill; Q20 criticised the old misleading message.
mandatory = [ghost]. Go: nothing to push, exit 0. Rust: hard error naming 'ghost', exit 3.
Go falls back to a walk and pushes (including untracked files). Rust: 'vault is not a git repository', exit 3, nothing written.
Go: git quotes the name, stat fails, project copies wiped. Rust uses git ls-files -z: the file is copied, exit 0.
Go: escaped name "\303\274n\303\257.md", stat fails, project copies wiped. Rust (-z) copies ünï.md, exit 0.
Go: RemoveAll removes languages/* then fails. Rust: the swap fails with EACCES (hint now blames permissions), project-a's copy stays complete, other targets sync, exit 4.
Go: stat error after wiping the project copy (partial tree). Rust: whole skill refused up front, project copies untouched.
Go copies the content of a file outside the vault through a tracked symlink. Rust fails the skill, exit 4, nothing copied.
Go: 'is a directory' error after wiping, leaves an empty file 'linkdir'. Rust: skill refused up front, project copies untouched.
Go dereferences a tracked file symlink into a regular file. Rust fails that skill ('contains a tracked symlink: link.md'), exit 4, project copies untouched.
Go wipes the project copy, then fails on the missing file (partial tree). Rust: 'tracked file ... is missing from the vault working tree', skill untouched, exit 4.
Go falls back to a walk (untracked files in, symlinks and build/ out). Rust: hard error, exit 3, nothing written.
Go wipes matching project copies and reports ok with 0 files. Rust fails that skill (exit 4) and keeps the project copy; the other skills sync.
Go counts tracked symlinks as files. Rust marks the skill failed ('contains a tracked symlink'), other skills are planned, exit 4 (rust_Rewrite.md §2 now says the same).
Go counts untracked files in the fallback walk. Rust: 'vault is not a git repository', exit 3.
SKILL_MANAG_EXCLUDE_DIRS: Go feeds exclude_dirs from the environment. Rust: any SKILL_MANAG_* variable is a hard error (exit 3) with a hint to use config.yaml.

exclude_dirs: [projects] matches the scan root's own name. Go skips the whole walk (nothing found). Rust does not apply directory exclusions to the root itself, so all 12 targets are found. Q11 describes the same flaw for the built-in prune list.
Go ignores an empty exclude_paths entry and an empty exclude_dirs name. Rust: 'exclude_paths has an empty entry' / 'exclude_dirs entry "" must be a bare directory name', exit 3.
Go ignores entries that match nothing (relative `no/such/dir`, absolute `<TMP>/nope`). Rust: 'exclude_paths entry ... does not exist', exit 3, for both.
This scenario matched in round 1. Its entries `../elsewhere` and `/nonexistent/abs` do not exist, so Rust now exits 3 where Go ignores them.
Go treats any vault subdir, dot-dirs included, as a skill (.hidden matched). Rust discovery skips dot-directories; .hidden is not a skill, so the project's .hidden copy is not a target.
Dry run. Go lists the skill as 'would sync (0 files)' (exit 0). Rust marks the skill failed (zero tracked files is a hard error for that skill) and exits 4; the other skills are planned.
Go `delete` without a name opens a TUI. Rust requires <NAME> (usage error, exit 2); no interactive delete in the CLI cut.
Go list is a TUI and fails without TTY. Rust `list` is a plain non-interactive listing, exit 0.

column4: Go opens the menu TUI (fails without TTY, exit 1). Rust now prints its help and exits 2 when no subcommand is given; there is no menu yet.
